Team — forwarding EnableBio's ask (quoted below). High level: prospect wants private deployment + 24mo commitment and is asking for ~40% off list. This would be outside our standard enterprise exercise for on-prem packaging and exceeds current discount guardrails for a deal this size.

Why I think it's strategic: EnableBio is a well-funded clinical data platform with immediate need for private inference and potential to expand to semantic search + embeddings across multiple product lines. They are currently evaluating two other vendors; pricing is the differentiator.

Proposed structuring to reduce downside:
- 30% headline discount on list for Year 1, stepping to 20% Year 2 (blended ~25%).
- Require 24-month upfront commitment with a 12-month non-cancellable minimum and an annual true-up.
- Add a 10% prepayment credit if they sign within 14 days.
- Constrain pilot to dedicated VPC with standard retention; any additional compliance work (e.g., fedramp-like controls) to be scoped and billed separately.

I attached a short business case and our proposed rate card to show margin impact. Asking for executive sign-off (VP/CFO) to authorize deviation from policy and to approve the discount exception memo we would send to the customer.

Next steps I recommend: VP/CFO review + legal signoff on T&C redlines (esp. data residency and audit requirements). If approved, I will push a signed LOI and DocuSign URL.

Lukas —

Thanks for the context and the proposed structure. A few quick questions before I sign off or push this:
1) What is the expected blended gross margin at the proposed blended ~25% effective discount? Need a clear number (percent) and ARR delta to model impact on Q3 guidance.
2) Is the 24-month minimum non-cancellable? We prefer a 12-month non-cancellable with a contractual true-up to protect revenue, otherwise exposure is high.
3) Any special commitments on SLAs/ops that would create cost pressure (SLA credits, bespoke support staffing)?

Alternative option: instead of moving to a full percentage discount, consider a structured credit (one-time onboarding credit tied to achieving commit milestones) + lower headline discount. That preserves list pricing reference and is simpler from a margin-control perspective.

Legal (Mina) — please confirm any material legal concerns on data residency wording or PO terms the customer will require.

If we can get margin numbers and a revised structure with milestone-based credits, I'll take to CFO for sign-off.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole

Marissa — quick follow up with the margin calc and a revised concession.

Margin impact (high level):
- List ARR: $1.2M/year
- Proposed blended effective ARR (our revised): Year1 $840k (30% off), Year2 $960k (20% off blended ~25% -> avg $900k)
- Estimated blended gross margin: ~42% (vs. standard target 55%) given dedicated VPC + increased support SLA (estimated incremental OpEx ~ $180k/yr).

Revised concession (to try to meet both sides):
- Headline: 25% blended discount across 24 months.
- Structure: 15% off Year1, 35% off Year2, plus a $75k onboarding credit applied in Year1. Credit tied to PO execution and a milestone (production go-live within 90 days).
- Cancellation: 12-month non-cancellable minimum with a 12-month true-up on remaining commitment if they churn after Month 12.
- SLA: Standard enterprise SLA; bespoke 24/7 support priced at cost with a $20k/yr premium (customer accepts).

I prefer the credit + blended path Marissa suggested; it preserves list for comps and reduces near-term margin hit. If you greenlight this path I will push the LOI and get DocuSign started.
